handled.claude-opus-5-thinking-off: Thinking off sends disabled with a chosen effort among low, medium and high only (ReasoningSettings), never the model's default. The visible-output risk is not measured here: the app reads its commands from the answer's text, so a leaked tag would surface as a parse failure.
handled.claude-sonnet-5-5-effort-recalibrated: The effort is the user's choice among the levels Anthropic's model list declares for the model (capabilities.effort); nothing in the app assumes what a level produces. No effort chosen keeps the model's default.
handled.claude-sonnet-5-5-thinking-between-tools: Thinking off is read from the thinking_off fact claude-sonnet-5-5-thinking-off: between_tools, offered only with an effort it accepts (low to high), always sent with one. disabled is never sent to this model. Its thinking blocks are skipped for the text block; no tool use, commands travel in the text, so the effort never changes within a conversation.
handled.claude-sonnet-5-5-thinking-off: Thinking off sends between_tools with a chosen effort among low, medium and high only; no tool use, so the answer is its text block.
handled.claude-thinking-always-on: These models offer no thinking off in the config screen (ReasoningSettings.of drops a fact whose thinking is null); saving thinking off for them is refused.
handled.claude-thinking-off-disabled: Thinking off sends disabled, at any effort chosen. With thinking on, no thinking field is sent: the 4.x models then run without thinking, as before.
handled.deepseek-default-effort-unknown: Never relied on: an effort is always chosen for a DeepSeek config (MessagesApi.DEEPSEEK effortRequired), checked at saving (ReasoningSettings.error).
handled.deepseek-effort-levels: Read by the app from its copy (ProviderFacts.effortLevels): the DeepSeek config offers these levels only, and saving refuses another.
handled.deepseek-thinking-off: Thinking off sends {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}} on the Anthropic-format endpoint, with the effort the config always has.
handled.deepseek-v4-flash-retired: The app names no model; a provider config saved with this ID keeps it. If the answer's model field then names V4.1-Flash, the call fails as a substitution (verifiesAnsweringModel), plainly; not measured. The free-models bench's deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash is OpenRouter's listing, still offered there apart from deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash at its own price (2026-10-02): kept.
handled.deepseek-v4-pro-served-by-flash: The app names no model: the user picks one from DeepSeek's own list, which still offers deepseek-v4-pro; until V4.1-Pro launches, choosing it gets V4.1-Flash, and nothing in the app says so.
